group.title: Colors and shapes
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: The color of the sun or a lemon.
wrong: The night sky is yellow and black.

words.meaning: The color between red and yellow, like a carrot.
wrong: The grass is bright orange in spring.

words.meaning: A light red color.
wrong: Snow is pink and cold.

words.meaning: A color made of red and blue.
wrong: Milk is purple and white.

words.meaning: The color of chocolate or wood.
wrong: Snow is brown and white.

words.meaning: The color between black and white, like rain clouds.
wrong: The gray sun is shining in the blue sky.

words.meaning: Having a bright yellow color like a ring or a coin.
wrong: Her gold dress is dark green.

words.meaning: Having a shiny gray color like a spoon or a coin.
wrong: The silver box is bright red.

words.meaning: Having many bright colors.
examples: The garden is full of {colorful} flowers.
wrong: The colorful picture is all gray.

words.meaning: The highest part of something.
examples: Write your name at the {top} of the page.
wrong: The top of the box is the part on the floor.

words.meaning: Smooth and giving back light.
wrong: The shiny car is dirty and dull.

words.meaning: The outside form of something, like round or square.
wrong: Red is my favorite shape.

words.meaning: A round shape like the letter O.
wrong: A circle has four straight sides.

words.meaning: A shape with four equal sides.
wrong: A square has only three sides.

words.meaning: A shape with three straight sides.
wrong: A triangle is as round as a ball.

words.meaning: A shape with four sides, two long and two short.
wrong: A rectangle has five round sides.

words.meaning: A shape like an egg.
wrong: An oval has three sharp corners.

words.meaning: A solid shape with six square sides, like a dice.
examples: Put an ice {cube} in my drink.
wrong: A cube is flat like a piece of paper.

words.meaning: A long thin mark.
wrong: A line is a big round spot.

words.meaning: A very small round mark.
examples: Put a {dot} at the end of the sentence.
wrong: The dot is so big it covers the whole page.

words.meaning: A long thin band of color.
wrong: A stripe is a round spot of color.

words.meaning: A small round mark of a different color.
examples: The dog has a black {spot} on its back.
wrong: The spot covers the whole wall.

words.meaning: A sign like a line with a point that shows a direction.
wrong: The arrow points in no direction.

words.meaning: A shape with four equal sides that stands on one corner.
wrong: A diamond is a round shape with no corners.

words.meaning: A colored stick of wax that children draw with.
examples: The child draws with a green {crayon}.
wrong: I eat soup with a crayon.

words.meaning: Shaped like a circle or a ball.
wrong: The round box has four sharp corners.

words.meaning: Having only black, white and gray, with no other colors.
examples: We watched an old {black and white} film.
wrong: The black and white photo is full of red and green.

words.meaning: Very, very small.
examples: A {tiny} ant is on my hand.
wrong: The tiny elephant is as big as a house.

words.meaning: Very, very big.
wrong: The huge mouse fits in my pocket.

words.meaning: Lines, shapes or colors repeated on something.
examples: Her dress has a {pattern} of red spots.
wrong: The plain white wall has a busy pattern.

words.meaning: Big in size.
wrong: The large shoe is too small for a baby.

words.meaning: Not big and not small.
wrong: Medium is the biggest size of all.

words.meaning: A shape with a square base and three-sided walls that meet at the top.
examples: The children built a {pyramid} of blocks.
wrong: A pyramid is as round as a ball.

words.meaning: The lowest part of something.
examples: Sign your name at the {bottom} of the page.
wrong: The bottom of the hill is its highest point.

words.meaning: A shape that is round at one end and pointed at the other.
examples: I had ice cream in a {cone}.
wrong: A cone is flat and square like a card.

words.meaning: Very, very big.
examples: There is a {giant} tree in the park.
wrong: The giant ant is too small to see.

words.meaning: One of two equal parts of something.
wrong: Half of the cake is all of it.

words.meaning: The part in the center of something.
examples: Stand in the {middle} of the room.
wrong: The middle is the very end of the line.

words.meaning: The left or right part of something.
examples: There is a door on the {side} of the house.
wrong: The side of the box is its top.

words.meaning: The outside line or end of something.
examples: Don’t stand near the {edge} of the table.
wrong: The edge of the plate is in its middle.
